transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As part of the normal prepayment review for the proposed $8,000,000 voluntary loan prepayment this quarter, I need to check with each of you before I make the binding treasury decision. We currently have $18,000,000 in unrestricted cash, a $10,000,000 term loan at 7.2%, and a $5,000,000 interest-rate swap paired with it. Before I approve the prepayment and release the payment and hedge instructions, I need to know: from lender relations, are there any prepayment penalties, notice requirements, or consent issues? From treasury forecasting, will an $8,000,000 outflow leave us with sufficient liquidity and do we need to adjust the swap? And from tax accounting, are there any tax implications — break costs, deductibility, or accounting treatment — that I should factor in? Please share anything relevant.

transcript.text: I completed the rolling cash forecast this morning, and it confirms that $7,250,000 of unrestricted cash must remain as the operating reserve through quarter-end due to scheduled payroll, tax, and supplier outflows. This forecast has not yet been circulated to Elena. With $18,000,000 in unrestricted cash, an $8,000,000 prepayment would leave us with $10,000,000, which covers the $7,250,000 reserve — but with only $2,750,000 of headroom. A $6,000,000 prepayment would leave $12,000,000, providing $4,750,000 of headroom above the reserve, which is a more comfortable liquidity buffer.
